method: Each line is one chord: four notes in soprano, alto, tenor, bass order. A note token is a letter A-G, an optional single sharp or flat, and an octave digit, so C4 is middle C and Bb3 is the B flat below it. Tokens are converted to MIDI note numbers with C4 = 60 and no double accidentals are accepted. Bar lines split chords within a line, blank lines are skipped, and one to eight chords are checked. The checker applies mechanical part-writing rules only. Ranges: soprano C4-C6 (60-84), alto G3-E5 (55-76), tenor C3-G4 (48-67), bass E2-C4 (40-60); a note outside its voice's range is reported. Crossing: in every chord the soprano must not sit below the alto, the alto not below the tenor, and the tenor not below the bass. Spacing: soprano to alto and alto to tenor must stay within twelve semitones; the tenor-bass gap is not limited. Overlap: across consecutive chords a voice must not move past the previous note of its neighbour, so an alto above the previous soprano note, or a soprano below the previous alto note, is reported. Parallels: for each of the six voice pairs an interval of a unison/octave or a perfect fifth that stays the same between consecutive chords is reported when both voices move and move in the same direction; a voice that repeats a note, or two voices moving in opposite directions, are not parallel. Intervals compare pitch classes, so a fifth displaced by an octave still counts as a fifth. The first chord has no previous chord, so no parallel or overlap check runs on it. There is no key, chord identification, doubling, dissonance or harmonic analysis, no voice-exchange or hidden-octave check, and no style judgement. Everything is computed in the browser; nothing is stored, uploaded or sent anywhere.
